newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bank bailout could cost $25 bln - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bank bailout could cost $25 bln - analyst.

text.p: The cost of Mexico's bank bailout programme could eventually reach 12 percent of the country's GDP, or about $25 billion, the New York-based Weston Group said on Thursday.

Correcting figures cited earlier by Weston analyst Andrew Balbus at a conference on global investment management in Mexico City, Weston director of research Fernando Losada told Reuters that the estimate of 12 percent of GDP would have to be assumed by the government over the next 10 years.
The Mexican government has initiated several programmes to help debtors meet their obligations following the 1994-95 peso crisis.
The net present-value costs of the bank bailout would be approximately $7 billion from the government's Bank Fund for Savings Protection (Fobaproa), Losada said.

In addition, he said the Weston Group estimates there are another $4 billion in non-performing mortgage loans, $3 billion in bad credit union loans, $1 billion in unrecoverable agricultural loans and $10 billion in unrecoverable development bank loans.

"It should be noted that these figures depend strongly on parameters that are unknown at the moment, as the effective recovery rates of problem loans," Losada said. "Thus, these figures have to be interpreted with extreme care."
